cohort: 200 pregnant women with pregnancy-induced hypertension and 200 normotensive pregnant women
finding: Pregnancy-induced hypertension was associated with a higher rate of cesarean delivery, intensive care admission, and adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the mode of delivery for 53% of women with pregnancy induced hypertension compared to 26% of normotensive cases.
birth_weight: Low birth weight in 62 (32.98%) neonates in the pregnancy-induced hypertension group
